ticket.title: Name 7 – Preview/Live Route Mismatch, 404 & Version Tracking
ticket.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 9

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Name 9's Workspace

#### Screenshot

#### What are you trying to achieve?

Name 18 needs to reliably preview and publish his Company One website, including an internal fictional assessment report at /internal/assessment-preview-fictional. He also needs to identify which website revision is currently previewed or deployed, while maintaining the intended access restrictions for internal report pages.

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

We want to ensure Name 9's Company One website publishes correctly, particularly the internal fictional assessment report at /internal/assessment-preview-fictional, which currently works in the Acquisity preview but returns a 404 error on the live domain.

We also need to resolve the reported node:crypto preview error, clarify how website revisions beyond Version 50 are tracked, and ensure that internal assessment pages remain properly access-restricted.

#### What is happening instead?

What is happening instead?
 Copy
We reproduced a preview-versus-live discrepancy. The fictional assessment report renders correctly in the Acquisity preview environment, but the same path on the published custom domain returns a 404 error. Name 18 also reports intermittent 'Failed to load node:crypto' errors referencing /lib/client-reports/access, and cannot track internal revisions beyond the displayed Version 50. He previously observed the assessment URL displaying the homepage instead of the intended report.

Steps to reproduce
 Copy

1. Open Name 9's Acquisity workspace and Name 7.
2. Open the Live project with ID <uuid>.
3. Open the website preview at <url> — the fictional assessment report renders successfully.
4. Open <url> in an incognito window — it returns '404: This page could not be found.'
5. Open the Version dropdown — Version 50 is marked Live, with a timestamp of 08:05 AM. Name 18 reports that subsequent internal revisions are not clearly identifiable.
6. Review the builder conversation for Name 18's reported node:crypto preview import failure.

#### What is the expected outcome?

The correct, authorized assessment route should be included in the published deployment and render consistently according to its intended access restrictions. Preview and published behavior should be consistent, and users should be able to identify the revision being previewed and deployed.

relatedSnapshot.title: Transient full-page 404 flashes on an already-loaded dashboard for legitimate members (getOrganizationBySlug swallows transient errors → notFound)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Name 2 investigation

Source: Lucent finding 87ec08db (Medium, AI Verified, 1 session) — user <email> on `/dashboard/<workspace-slug>`. A full-page `404 - Page Not Found` flashes for ~1s **after the dashboard has already rendered**, then the dashboard reappears on its own. No user navigation precedes the flash.

**Finding:** Bug — a *transient* backend failure inside `getOrganizationBySlug` is silently converted into a hard full-page 404 for a user who is genuinely a member, and the event is invisible to all monitoring.

### Root cause (code)

* Name 3 layout `apps/web/app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/[organizationSlug]/layout.tsx:36-39` and the dashboard page `.../[organizationSlug]/page.tsx:30-33` both do `const org = await getOrganizationBySlug(slug); if (!org) return notFound();`.
* `getOrganizationBySlug` (`apps/web/lib/auth/server.ts:355-416`) wraps `auth.api.getFullOrganization()` + a follow-up `organizationTable` query in a `try/catch` whose catch (`412-414`) maps **any** thrown error to `null` with **no** `logger.error` **and no Sentry capture**.
* Net effect: `null` conflates three very different cases — (a) org doesn't exist, (b) user is not a member, (c) a transient error (auth-DB/network blip, session-cookie rotation race, or an aborted/re-issued RSC render). All three render a hard `notFound()`. When (c) happens during a background RSC re-render of the layout, the whole page flips to 404 and self-heals on the next successful render.

### Why this is a member-facing bug, not user error

Prod read-only DB: <email> (`<uuid>`, global role `customer_success`) is an **owner** member of Company Two (`cd0664ee-...`, slug `<workspace-slug>`), one of 7 org memberships. She is unambiguously a member, so the `null` return here was a false negative from a transient failure — not a real "not found"/"not a member".

### Observability gap (part of the bug)

Because the catch is silent, these 404 flashes leave **no trace**:

* Sentry: no server-side exception on this path (swallowed). The only related signal is the unrelated "Not a member of the organization" family thrown from other code paths.
* Axiom (`acquisity`, 30d): zero `getFullOrganization` / `getOrganizationBySlug` / `notFound` logs; zero logs referencing `<workspace-slug>` or the user id for the replay window. (The 120 "User is not a member of the organization for this billing account" logs are a different, billing-account path.)
  So the true frequency of these transient 404s is currently unknowable.

### Finding classification

**Bug** — chosen over User Error (user is a legitimate owner member) and Platform Limitation (self-inflicted error-swallowing, not a provider limit).

### Decision

Engineering Todo (Low)

### Routing

* Project: Core Platform
* Assignee: Anuj Bhatt
* Status: Todo
* Priority: Low
* Assignment changed: Yes
* Final action: Routed to owner
* Confidence: Medium (root cause of the *symptom* is certain; the exact re-render trigger is not recoverable from an 8s replay with zero server logs)

### Evidence checked

* Lucent get_issue/list_issues: Medium, aiVerified, sessionCount=1.
* Session replay frames: dashboard fully rendered (0-3s) → full-page 404 (~4s) → dashboard back (~5s); NPS "Quick feedback" popup appears coincidentally; no user navigation before the flash.
* Prod DB: user is customer_success + owner member of the org; 7 memberships (legit member).
* Sentry: no matching swallowed-path exception.
* Axiom: no getOrganizationBySlug/notFound logs; confirms silent path.
* Name 1: related to ENG-11414 (non-member redirect → permanent 404, In Progress) and ENG-2672 (swallowed errors invisible in Sentry). Distinct from ENG-11310/ENG-11308 (onboarding-completion redirect race).

### Recommended next step

1. In `getOrganizationBySlug`, stop swallowing everything into `null`. Distinguish "genuinely absent / not a member" (→ `null` → `notFound()`) from a thrown transient error: `logger.error({ slug, error }, ...)` + capture to Sentry, and rethrow (or return a distinct sentinel) so the layout can render an error/retry boundary instead of a hard 404. This both fixes the member-facing hard-404 and closes the observability gap so the re-render trigger can be captured next time.
2. With logging in place, correlate future occurrences to pin the exact re-render trigger (background RSC refresh vs auth session rotation vs aborted RSC stream — cf. the frequent "Invalid state: Controller is already closed" streaming errors).

### Potential fix, if engineering bug

Same `getOrganizationBySlug` remediation described above; overlaps with ENG-11414's graceful-degradation work — consider folding if that PR already touches this function.

### Triage scope confirmation

No branch, commit, PR, deployment, migration, patch, code/docs/config change, or other implementation action was created in this session.

relatedSnapshot.title: Sign-in redirectTo to an inaccessible workspace lands on a hard 404 dead-end
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Name 2 investigation

Source: Lucent finding dc3b9671 (Medium, AI Verified, 1 session) — user <email> (internal admin) signed in and was redirected to a workspace-settings URL, landing on a hard `404 - Page Not Found` dead-end.

**Finding:** Bug (UX / graceful-degradation gap) — after sign-in, the app redirects to the `redirectTo` target with no validation that the target org slug is accessible to the just-signed-in user. When it isn't, the org-settings layout hard-404s with no recovery path other than the "Back to Home" button.

**Decision:** Engineering Todo

### Root cause (code-level)

1. `apps/web/proxy.ts:788` — for any unauthenticated `/dashboard/*` request, middleware redirects to `/auth/sign-in?redirectTo=${pathname}${search}`, capturing whatever org-scoped path the user was on (e.g. `/dashboard/<slug>/settings/...`).
2. `apps/web/components/auth/sign-in-card.tsx:84-106` — `getRedirectPath()` blindly trusts `redirectTo` and does `router.replace(redirectPath)` after sign-in. No check that the target org is one the freshly-signed-in session can access.
3. `apps/web/app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/(organization-settings)/[organizationSlug]/settings/layout.tsx:24-27` — calls `getOrganizationBySlug(slug)`; on null it returns `notFound()` → the 404 screen.
4. `apps/web/lib/auth/server.ts:355-416` — `getOrganizationBySlug` calls Name 4 `auth.api.getFullOrganization({ query: { organizationSlug } })`, which throws `Not a member of the organization` when the session user isn't a member of that slug's org. The `catch (_error) { return null }` at line 412-414 swallows it silently (so this 404 never reaches Sentry).

Net effect: signing in with a `redirectTo` pointing at a workspace the user is not a member of (stale/renamed slug, a workspace they were viewing via impersonation that has since expired, or removed membership) produces a dead-end 404 instead of a graceful fallback to the user's own dashboard / workspace picker.

**Routing:**

* Project: Core Platform
* Assignee: Anuj Bhatt
* Status: Todo
* Priority: Low
* Assignment changed: Yes
* Final action: Routed to owner (Core Platform)
* Confidence: Medium (mechanism confirmed in code + Sentry "Not a member" throw pattern; exact `redirectTo` slug not recoverable from the DOM-only Lucent replay)

**Evidence checked:**

* Prod DB (read-only): user 851a5a0f… <email> is role=admin, member/owner of only 4 orgs. Latest session e723f504 was a fresh sign-in at 2026-07-10T06:32Z (active org `<workspace-slug>`, impersonated_by=null); replay ~07:05Z. An admin routinely reaches workspaces outside her own membership, so a `redirectTo` to a non-member slug is plausible.
* Sentry: ACQUISITY-40Z "Not a member of the organization" (culprit `apps/web/lib/auth/server.ts`, 13 users / 6639 events, ongoing) confirms `getFullOrganization` throws exactly this for non-member org lookups. Sampled events are the tRPC/preview variant, not the settings-layout path — consistent with the settings-layout 404 being silently swallowed and invisible to Sentry.
* Axiom (`acquisity`): no log for the null-return path — `getOrganizationBySlug` swallows the error without logging, so frequency can't be sized from logs.
* Name 1: ENG-3686 "Show organization membership error instead of 404 page" (Done, Athena-era) is the exact prior-art ask for this graceful-handling behavior; the behavior still exists in the current app. Distinct from the onboarding-redirect race (ENG-11310 In Progress; ENG-11308 folded in as Duplicate), which is triggered by a just-created org, not a sign-in `redirectTo`.

**Recommended next step:**

* Validate/guard the post-sign-in redirect: before `router.replace(redirectTo)`, verify the target org slug is in the user's accessible org list, else fall back to `appConfig.auth.redirectAfterSignIn` (or last-active workspace / workspace picker).
* And/or make the `[organizationSlug]` layouts render a "you don't have access to this workspace" state (per ENG-3686) instead of a bare `notFound()`, and add a `logger.warn` in `getOrganizationBySlug`'s catch so this stops being invisible.

**Potential fix, if engineering bug:**

* In `sign-in-card.tsx` `getRedirectPath()`, resolve org slug from `redirectTo` and cross-check against `getOrganizationList()`/accessible orgs; sanitize to the default dashboard when not accessible. Mirror the ENG-3686 membership-error component in the org-scoped layouts as defense-in-depth.

**Triage scope confirmation:**
No branch, commit, PR, deployment, migration, patch, code/docs/config change, or other implementation action was created in this session.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI Name 7 publish of <domain> fails with 'Publishing failed' after a failed production build, and the build error is never surfaced
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Intercom conversation**: <url:app.intercom.com>

**Testable claim**: A customer on a website whose custom domain <domain> shows verified and connected (website.domainVerified = true, domain_verified_at 2026-09-17T13:22:05Z) cannot publish version 26; every publish shows only "Publishing failed. Please try again." while version 19, the last successful deploy, still reports as published, so the button flips between Publish and Update. The site's production deployment is stuck at deployment_status = failed with deployment_error `Command "bun run build" exited with 1` (vercel_deployment_id dpl_5NoSQNGf5cxHXbZ9PovBartdYscX, updated 2026-09-18T15:54:36Z), and the customer reports no deployment logs to troubleshoot.

**Bounded conversation context**: Opened 2026-09-18 15:41 UTC, tagged AI Name 7, agent Fin AI then assigned to Name 8. The customer states: publishing changes throws "publishing failed"; there is no "Fix with AI" option; the panel shows only the generic "Publishing failed. Please try again."; "We could not load your domain ownership"; the last successful deploy was version 19 (the first publish), selecting version 19 shows published and the button reads Update, while selecting version 26 and pressing update changes the button to Publish and fails; no deployment logs are visible to troubleshoot; asking the in-product AI to rebuild with no design changes charged 275+ credits and produced no rebuild and no new version, leaving them about 280 credits down. Two screenshots show the <domain> domain modal with a green Connected badge and the banner "We could not load your domain ownership. Retry before removing this domain."

**Evidence snapshot (2026-09-18, commit 36f37d386abadd67452b6889cf446ef226fad560)**: website row deployment_status = failed, deployment_error `Command "bun run build" exited with 1`, custom_domain <domain>, domain_verified true. Blast radius from production: 20 live website rows across 18 organizations are in deployment_status failed, 7 of those organizations also carry a verified custom domain. Code path: `publishWebsiteDeployment` in apps/web/lib/website/publish-website-deployment.ts persists deploymentStatus 'pending' in the same update that stores the new vercelDeploymentId; `website.checkDeploymentStatus` in apps/web/trpc/routers/website/web-core.ts writes 'failed' with the provider error message; the redeploy-after-domain-connect Inngest function returns mode 'skip' whenever deploymentStatus is 'failed'. The customer-facing message is a constant, PUBLISHED_WEBSITE_SAFE_DEPLOYMENT_ERROR in apps/web/lib/website/published-website-url.ts returned by getWebsiteDeploymentErrorMessage for any failed deployment, which discards the persisted build error; apps/web/components/ai-website-creator/publish-control.tsx renders it. Overlapping open work: parent master ENG-13921 and its child ENG-13920 cover the never-published plus verified-domain-shown-as-connected coupling, ENG-12240 and the canceled SAN-42 cover this exact publish failure string, and ENG-10093 covers hardening the publish flow.

relatedSnapshot.title: Inngest: 401 sending events to archived preview environment
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Bug

Name 11 handler at `lib/webhooks/outreach/inngest-routing.ts:80` attempts to send events to an Inngest preview environment that has been archived. The environment is no longer active but the webhook routing still targets it.

---

## Root Cause

Three mechanisms combine:

1. **Vercel bakes** `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_REF` into preview deployments — the branch name persists in the deployment even after the branch is deleted.
2. **Inngest archives** preview environments when the associated branch is deleted.
3. **Name 11 routing** uses `inngest.send()` directly without checking whether the target environment is still active.

---

## Codebase Verification

Confirmed in codebase:

* `lib/inngest/index.ts`: `inngest` client initialized with a single `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` — no per-environment routing in application code
* `lib/webhooks/outreach/inngest-routing.ts`: all `inngest.send()` calls go through the single client with no environment health check
* The 401 originates from Inngest's cloud infrastructure rejecting the event key for an archived environment
* No deterministic application-level fix exists: catch-and-drop risks silent data loss; pre-flight health check adds latency and a new API dependency; infrastructure prevention requires Vercel/Inngest lifecycle hooks outside the codebase

## Agent Feasibility

**Not suitable for agent.** Requires a deployment topology decision (Vercel + Inngest lifecycle configuration) before any code change. No unit-testable fix exists in the application layer. The fix lives in Vercel/Inngest project settings, not in this repository.

relatedSnapshot.title: Store preview, publish, and version history
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Build Store Preview and Publish Flow — Version History with Rollback ### Context This feature complements the store builder editor (ENG-7115) by adding a complete publish workflow: preview draft changes before going live, version history tracking with every publish, and the ability to rollback to any previous version. This ensures store owners can confidently make changes knowing they can always revert if something goes wrong. The publish flow follows a **draft → preview → publish** pattern where all edits are saved as drafts, previewed in context, and only made live when the user explicitly publishes. Each publish creates a versioned snapshot that can be restored later. --- ### Database Schema **New table:** `commerceStoreVersion` — add to `lib/db/schema/commerce.ts`: ```typescript export const commerceStoreVersionTable = pgTable( 'commerce_store_version', { ...getBaseColumnsWithOrganization(), pageId: uuid('page_id').notNull().references(() => commerceStorePageTable.id, { onDelete: 'cascade' }), version: integer('version').notNull(), // auto-incrementing per page, calculated as MAX(version) + 1 sections: jsonb('sections').$type().notNull(), // full snapshot of sections at publish time publishedAt: timestamp('published_at', { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(), publishedBy: uuid('published_by').references(() => userTable.id, { onDelete: 'set null' }), }, (table) => [ index('commerce_store_version_page_idx').on(table.pageId), uniqueIndex('commerce_store_version_page_version_idx').on(table.pageId, table.version), ] ); ``` **Key design decisions:** * `version` is an integer that auto-increments per page (not globally) — calculated at insert time via `SELECT MAX(version) + 1` * `sections` stores a complete JSONB snapshot of the sections array at the time of publish — no diffs, full snapshot for simplicity and reliable rollback * `publishedBy` references the user who triggered the publish, with `SET NULL` on delete so versions survive user deletion * `pageId` has `CASCADE` delete — if the page is deleted, all its versions are cleaned up * Unique index on `(pageId, version)` prevents duplicate version numbers * Follows the same pattern as `websiteVersionTable` in `lib/db/schema/website-version.ts` **Relation to** `commerceStorePageTable` (from ENG-7115): * `commerceStorePageTable.publishedVersionId` references the currently live version * `commerceStorePageTable.sections` = the live sections (copied from draft at publish time) * `commerceStorePageTable.draftSections` = in-progress edits (null when no unpublished changes) --- ### tRPC Procedures **Extend** `trpc/routers/commerce/store-builder.ts` with these additional procedures: #### `publishPage` (mutation) Full publish flow — this is the most critical procedure: ``` Input: { slug: string } Steps: 1. Get current page by slug + orgId (from context) 2. Verify draftSections is not null (there must be unpublished changes to publish) 3. Calculate next version number: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1 FROM commerce_store_version WHERE page_id = ? 4. Insert version snapshot: INSERT INTO commerce_store_version (pageId, version, sections, publishedBy) VALUES (page.id, nextVersion, page.draftSections, ctx.user.id) 5. Update the page atomically: UPDATE commerce_store_page SET sections = draftSections, draftSections = NULL, isPublished = true, publishedAt = NOW(), publishedVersionId = newVersion.id WHERE id = page.id 6. Return { version: nextVersion, publishedAt: new Date() } ``` All steps should run in a single database transaction to ensure atomicity. #### `listVersions` (query) ``` Input: { pageId: string } Output: Array of { id, version, publishedAt, publishedBy: { id, name, image } } - Join on user table for publisher name and avatar - Sort by version DESC (newest first) - Paginate with cursor-based pagination (optional for MVP, limit 50) ``` #### `rollbackToVersion` (mutation) ``` Input: { versionId: string } Steps: 1. Load the version record by ID, verify it belongs to a page in the user's org 2. Set the version's sections as the page's draftSections: UPDATE commerce_store_page SET draftSections = version.sections WHERE id = version.pageId 3. Return the restored sections so the builder can immediately display them ``` **Important:** Rollback does NOT directly update the live `sections`. It loads the old version as a **draft** so the user can review and optionally edit before re-publishing. This prevents accidental live changes. #### `getPreviewData` (query) ``` Input: { slug: string } Output: { sections: StoreSection[], isPublished: boolean, hasDraft: boolean } - Returns draftSections if they exist (for preview), otherwise returns published sections - Used by the preview route/panel to render the current state ``` --- ### Publish Flow UI (in Store Builder) The publish controls live in a **toolbar** at the top of the store builder page, between the header and the three-panel layout. **Name 14 buttons:** | Button | Condition | Action | | -- | -- | -- | | **Save Draft** | Always visible | Explicitly saves current sections to `draftSections`. Note: auto-save (from ENG-7115) already handles this, but an explicit button provides user confidence. | | **Publish** | Active only when `draftSections !== null` (has unpublished changes) | Calls `publishPage` mutation → shows success toast "Published! Version X is now live." | | **Discard Changes** | Active only when `draftSections !== null` | Confirmation dialog: "Discard all unpublished changes? This will revert to the last published version." → calls `discardDraft` → reloads published sections into editor. | | **History** | Always visible | Opens the version history Sheet (right-side drawer). | | **Preview** | Always visible | Opens full-page preview in a new tab. | **Visual indicators:** * Show a badge/dot on the "Publish" button when there are unpublished changes * Show "Draft" badge in the toolbar when editing unpublished changes * Show "Published" badge with relative timestamp when no draft exists --- ### Version History UI **Component:** `components/commerce/store-builder/VersionHistorySheet.tsx` Opens as a `Sheet` (from ` at /components/ui/sheet`) sliding in from the right side, triggered by the "History" button in the toolbar. **Layout:** ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────┐ │ Version History [X] │ ├─────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ v3 (Current) LIVE │ │ │ │ Published 2 hours ago │ │ │ │ by Name 12 │ │ │ │ [Rollback] │ │ ← disabled for current version │ └─────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ v2 │ │ │ │ Published 3 days ago │ │ │ │ by Jane Smith │ │ │ │ [Rollback] │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ v1 │ │ │ │ Published Name 13 15, 2026 │ │ │ │ by Name 12 │ │ │ │ [Rollback] │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **Each version row shows:** * Version number (e.g., "v3") * "LIVE" badge (using ``) on the version matching `publishedVersionId` * Relative timestamp using `formatDistanceToNow` from `date-fns` (e.g., "2 hours ago", "3 days ago") * Publisher name and avatar * "Rollback" button — disabled for the currently live version **Rollback flow:** 1. User clicks "Rollback" on a version 2. Confirmation dialog appears: "Restore version X? This will load the sections from version X as a draft. You can review the changes and publish when ready." 3. On confirm: call `rollbackToVersion` mutation 4. Close the Sheet 5. Builder loads the restored sections as the current draft 6. User can now edit further or publish immediately 7. Show toast: "Version X restored as draft. Publish to make it live." --- ### Preview Implementation **Option A (Recommended for MVP): Name 15 preview in builder center panel** The center panel of the three-panel layout (from ENG-7115) already renders section renderers inline. This serves as the primary preview. No additional work needed for basic preview. **Option B: Full-page preview in new tab** For a more accurate representation of how the storefront will look: 1. **"Open Preview" button** in the toolbar opens a new browser tab 2. **Preview route:** `app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/[organizationSlug]/store-builder/preview/page.tsx` 3. This page renders a full-width storefront preview (no builder chrome) using `getPreviewData` 4. **Preview banner:** A fixed-position bar at the top of the preview page: ```tsx
Preview These changes are not live yet
``` 5. The preview page adds `padding-top` to account for the banner height 6. Preview renders `draftSections` if available, otherwise falls back to published `sections` --- ### Component Structure ``` components/commerce/store-builder/ ├── PublishToolbar.tsx — toolbar with Save Draft, Publish, Discard, History, Preview buttons ├── VersionHistorySheet.tsx — Sheet with version list, rollback actions ├── VersionHistoryItem.tsx — individual version row in the history list ├── RollbackConfirmDialog.tsx — confirmation dialog for rollback action ├── DiscardDraftDialog.tsx — confirmation dialog for discarding unpublished changes ├── PreviewBanner.tsx — fixed banner shown on full-page preview ("Changes are not live") └── PublishSuccessToast.tsx — (optional) custom toast content showing version number ``` --- ### State Management **Draft detection:** ```typescript const hasDraft = page.draftSections !== null; const isPublished = page.isPublished; ``` **Publish button state:** * Disabled when `!hasDraft` (nothing to publish) * Shows loading spinner during `publishPage` mutation * After success: invalidate `getPage` query, close any open editors, show toast **Optimistic updates:** * On publish: optimistically set `draftSections = null` and `sections = draftSections` in the query cache * On discard: optimistically set `draftSections = null` and reload `sections` from cache * On rollback: optimistically set `draftSections = restoredSections` in the query cache --- ### Codebase Reference Table | What | File | Pattern to Follow | | -- | -- | -- | | Version table pattern | `lib/db/schema/website-version.ts` | Status enum, snapshot JSONB storage, version numbering | | Deployment pattern | `lib/db/schema/website-deployment.ts` | Provider enum, status tracking (reference only) | | Preview panel | `components/website-builder/preview-panel.tsx` | iframe with sandbox, postMessage sync (for future iframe approach) | | Sheet component | ` at /components/ui/sheet` | Right-side drawer for version history | | Name 16 component | ` at /components/ui/dialog` | Rollback and discard confirmation dialogs | | Badge | ` at /components/ui/badge` | `variant="success"` for LIVE, `variant="warning"` for Draft/Preview | | Button | ` at /components/ui/button` | Name 14 buttons with variant and size props | | Toast | `sonner` / ` at /components/ui/sonner` | Success/error notifications | | formatDistanceToNow | `date-fns` | Relative timestamps in version history (e.g., "2 hours ago") | | Schema | `lib/db/schema/commerce.ts` | Add `commerceStoreVersionTable` alongside the page table | | tRPC router | `trpc/routers/commerce/store-builder.ts` | Extend with publish/version/rollback procedures | | Transaction pattern | Existing tRPC mutations | `db.transaction(async (tx) => { ... })` for atomic publish | | Page layout | ` at /components/ui/page` | `Page`, `PageHeader`, `PageBody` for preview page | | User join | `lib/db/schema/user.ts` | Join `userTable` for publisher name in version list | --- ### Implementation Steps 1. **Add** `commerceStoreVersionTable` to `lib/db/schema/commerce.ts` with the schema above. Export from `lib/db/schema/index.ts`. Define Drizzle relations to `commerceStorePageTable` and `userTable`. 2. **Run** `bun db:generate` to create the migration, then `bun db:migrate` to apply it. 3. **Add** `publishPage` procedure to the store builder tRPC router — implement the full 6-step publish flow inside a database transaction. 4. **Add** `listVersions` procedure — query with user join, sorted by version DESC. 5. **Add** `rollbackToVersion` procedure — load version, set as draftSections on the page. 6. **Add** `getPreviewData` procedure — return draftSections or sections based on availability. 7. **Build** `PublishToolbar.tsx` — toolbar component with all 5 buttons, proper disabled states, and loading indicators. 8. **Integrate toolbar** into `StoreBuilderPage.tsx` (from ENG-7115) — place between the page header and the three-panel layout. 9. **Build** `VersionHistorySheet.tsx` — Sheet component that fetches and displays version list. 10. **Build** `VersionHistoryItem.tsx` — individual version row with version number, relative date, publisher info, LIVE badge, and rollback button. 11. **Build** `RollbackConfirmDialog.tsx` — confirmation dialog with clear messaging about what rollback does (loads as draft, not direct publish). 12. **Build** `DiscardDraftDialog.tsx` — confirmation dialog for discarding unpublished changes. 13. **Implement rollback flow** — on confirm, call mutation, close sheet, update builder state, show toast. 14. **Build preview page** at `app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/[organizationSlug]/store-builder/preview/page.tsx` — full-width storefront rendering with preview banner. 15. **Build** `PreviewBanner.tsx` — fixed-position warning banner for preview mode. 16. **Add optimistic updates** — update TanStack Query cache on publish, discard, and rollback for instant UI feedback. 17. **Update** `scripts/dump-preview-data.sh` — add `dump_copy` lines for both `commerce_store_page` and `commerce_store_version` tables. 18. **Test the full publish cycle** — create draft → preview → publish → verify version created → rollback → verify draft loaded → re-publish. --- ### Verification Checklist - [ ] `commerceStoreVersionTable` migration runs cleanly on a fresh database - [ ] Unique index on `(pageId, version)` prevents duplicate version numbers - [ ] `publishPage` creates a version snapshot with correct version number (incrementing from previous max) - [ ] `publishPage` atomically updates `sections`, clears `draftSections`, sets `isPublished`, and links `publishedVersionId` - [ ] `publishPage` runs in a transaction — if any step fails, nothing is committed - [ ] `publishPage` rejects if `draftSections` is null (nothing to publish) - [ ] `listVersions` returns versions sorted newest-first with publisher name and avatar - [ ] `listVersions` correctly identifies the currently live version via `publishedVersionId` - [ ] `rollbackToVersion` loads old sections as `draftSections` (NOT directly to live `sections`) - [ ] `rollbackToVersion` verifies the version belongs to a page in the user's organization - [ ] Publish button is disabled when there are no unpublished changes - [ ] Discard Changes button is disabled when there are no unpublished changes - [ ] Rollback button is disabled for the currently live version in the history list - [ ] Confirmation dialogs appear before rollback and discard actions - [ ] Toast notifications show on publish success, rollback success, and discard success - [ ] Version history Sheet loads and displays all versions for the current page - [ ] Preview page renders draft sections with the preview warning banner - [ ] Preview banner clearly communicates that changes are not live - [ ] Optimistic updates provide instant feedback on publish/discard/rollback - [ ] `scripts/dump-preview-data.sh` updated with new tables - [ ] No ` at /lib/env` imports in any client components - [ ] All logging uses `logger` from ` at /lib/logger` (not console) - [ ] All database queries are scoped to the authenticated user's organization

relatedSnapshot.title: Announcement "AI Name 7 Creator is live" CTA leads to 404 for orgs with feature disabled
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Name 2 investigation

**Finding:** Bug — the global announcement "AI Name 7 Creator is live" (id `1027fa5b`) broadcasts to all users but its CTA "Check it out now!" links to `/dashboard/{{organizationSlug}}/sites`, which is feature-gated behind `AI_WEBSITE_CREATOR`. Users in 129 orgs with this feature explicitly disabled get a 404.

**Decision:** Engineering Todo

**Routing:**

* Project: Core Platform
* Assignee: Anuj Bhatt
* Status: Todo
* Priority: Low
* Assignment changed: Yes
* Final action: Routed to owner
* Confidence: High

**Evidence checked:**

* Prod DB: Announcement `1027fa5b` is published (June 5, 2026) with no expiration, no partner filter, and `show_in_whats_new: true`. CTA block href is `/dashboard/{{organizationSlug}}/sites`. 2,282 users have seen it. 129/7,452 orgs (1.7%) have `ai_website_creator: false` in workspace feature flags. 1 partner (Customer Workspace) also disables the feature.
* Codebase: `/sites` layout (`apps/web/app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/[organizationSlug]/sites/layout.tsx`) calls `requireOrganizationFeature(organizationSlug, FEATURES.AI_WEBSITE_CREATOR)` which returns `notFound()` when feature is disabled. The `AnnouncementProvider` does not filter announcements by feature flags of their CTA links.
* Name 1: ENG-7724 (Done) fixed the same pattern for the Billing page "Open Domains" button by conditionally rendering it based on `hasWebsiteCreator`. The announcement CTA was not covered.
* Sentry: MCP unavailable (401). No server-side exceptions expected since 404 is a `notFound()` from Next.js.
* Axiom: No error logs matching this pattern (404 is handled at the Next.js routing layer, not logged as an application error).

**Recommended next step:**

* Quick fix: Either set an expiration on the announcement, or update the CTA href to the ungated docs link (`<url:app.acquisity.ai>`) which already exists as the second CTA in the announcement.
* Systemic fix: Add feature-awareness to the announcement system so CTAs linking to feature-gated pages are hidden or disabled for users without the feature.

**Potential fix, if engineering bug:**

* Quick data fix: UPDATE the announcement content in the database to remove or change the CTA href, or set `expires_at` to a past date.
* Systemic: In `AnnouncementProvider` or the `getUnread` tRPC endpoint, filter out announcements whose CTA hrefs reference feature-gated routes when the user's workspace doesn't have those features. Alternatively, add a `requiredFeature` field to the announcement schema so admins can scope announcements to feature-enabled workspaces.

**Triage scope confirmation:**
No branch, commit, PR, deployment, migration, patch, code/docs/config change, or other implementation action was created in this session.

relatedSnapshot.title: First publish after copying a template fails with 404 — need to poll version readiness before deploying forked templates
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem Statement

When a user copies a template and publishes the website, the Vercel deployment almost always fails with a 404 page. Only after editing the website and publishing again does the build succeed.

## Impact

* **User Impact**: First publish after copying a template consistently fails — users see a "404 NOT_FOUND" page instead of their website and must manually edit + re-publish to get a working deployment.
* **Development Impact**: Frequent support questions about broken first deploys after template copy.

## Solution

Poll version readiness before deploying forked templates to ensure the Vercel project has the latest code available before triggering a deployment.

## Related PR

<url:github.com>

relatedSnapshot.title: Fix edit image version save behavior and stale preview state
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The image-editing flow has confusing save/version behavior and can leave stale previews visible until refresh. Users may think they saved a new version when the UI still shows the old one, or vice versa.

## Goal

By default you do not change the current version of the image after an edit and keep the existing version of the image as the current version and just show the new version of the image so that the user can decide if they want to make the new version the current version.

## Scope

* Explicit version save behavior
* Correct preview refresh after edits
* Clear relationship between original and new edited versions

## Acceptance criteria

* Saving an edited version behaves predictably
* The UI reflects the latest saved state without requiring manual refresh
* Users can tell which version is active

relatedSnapshot.title: Add guided expression builder with live preview and validation
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Template/expression authoring remains error-prone and less discoverable than n8n-style expression workflows.

## Root Cause

Expressions are supported, but authoring relies heavily on manual typing and post-failure correction rather than guided construction and live evaluation.

## Example of how it'll cause issues

A user references the wrong upstream field path, publishes successfully, then discovers failures at runtime due to invalid expression output.

## Plan for solution

1. Add expression builder UI with node/field picker and operator helpers.
2. Add live preview/evaluation using latest run data and/or mock input.
3. Add inline validation with actionable error messages before run/publish.
4. Support quick insert from output schema and copy-safe path generation.
5. Add unit/integration tests for expression serialization and preview correctness.

relatedSnapshot.title: In-app Store Builder live preview before Shopify deploy
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Goal

Add an in-app preview that shows the generated store before deploying to Shopify.

## Why

This is useful, but should likely come after the designer-led Store Builder UI redesign. It lets users inspect the starter store before deployment without needing to understand Shopify internals.

## Scope

* Render a close approximation of the generated storefront inside Acquisity.
* Show homepage, product page, key utility pages, navigation, colors, logo, CTAs, and product media.
* Surface readiness warnings directly on preview sections.

## Acceptance Criteria

* User can inspect the generated starter storefront before deployment.
* Preview reflects current draft and Brand Kit values.
* Preview highlights missing/broken content before deploy.
* This is implemented after, or in coordination with, the Store Builder UI redesign work.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI Name 7 publish of <domain> keeps failing and the build error is never shown: versions 34 and 36 fail while version 32 is live and version 34 builds on the customer's own Vercel account
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Intercom conversation**: <url:app.intercom.com>

**Testable claim**: On the Name 17 LLC Name 7 (website id <uuid>, vercel project <project-slug>, custom domain <domain> verified), publishing fails for website versions 34 and 36 while version 32 is live and deployed; the customer sees only the generic "Publishing failed. Please try again." and has no way to read the underlying Vercel build error. Production state on 2026-09-22: website.deployment_status = failed with deployment_error `Command "bun run build" exited with 2` (vercel_deployment_id dpl_41eE1ppWua4rZNbZF3VwatUG3rFp, updated 2026-09-22T01:25:51Z). The customer also reproduced version 34 successfully on his own personal Vercel account, so the failing step is the platform's production build, not the site code alone.

**Bounded conversation context**: Opened 2026-09-21 01:59 UTC. The customer asks for the first error in the Vercel build logs for version 34. Fin AI tells him the build error appears in the Publish / Update control and vanishes when he leaves the screen; he replies "it is not visible to me" and then "all it says is publishing failed. I want to see the error in the vercel build logs". Fin AI answers that Vercel build logs cannot be viewed from inside the app. He asks for a human at 02:02 UTC, again at 14:36 UTC, and at 01:07 UTC on 2026-09-22 after waiting more than 24 hours. Ellaine Fuente replies at 01:14 UTC and he supplies the detail: version 36 is current, version 32 deployed successfully and is live, version 34 failed with the AI editor's assistance, he ran version 34 successfully through his personal Vercel account, version 36 (a further AI edit) also failed, and he wants the build errors so he can correct the code. He notes that on the previous Saturday Aaron worked with him to resolve the same publish failure for version 26. Last message 2026-09-22 01:25 UTC: "are you able to share the error in vercel build log?" No attachments.

**Evidence collected**

* Production (PlanetScale, queried 2026-09-22): website deployment_status failed, deployment_error `Command "bun run build" exited with 2`; the row carries a production vercel_deployment_id, so a failed production build was recorded even though the customer reports version 32 as live.
* Code at commit 5da66710578f5abedc1c4ee8566676ad1ab0228d: `apps/web/lib/website/published-website-url.ts` `getWebsiteDeploymentErrorMessage` returns the fixed string "Publishing failed. Please try again." for any failed deployment and never exposes `deploymentError`; `apps/web/lib/website-agent/deployment-status.ts` `resolveAgentGitDeploymentStatus` maps a Vercel ERROR state into that persisted deployment_error. The UI has no path to the build log, matching what Fin AI told the customer.
* Related: the same workspace and site already have a customer report under the same master, and no account, campaign, or provider lane applies here.
* Lane could not run: Vercel build events for dpl_41eE1ppWua4rZNbZF3VwatUG3rFp returned HTTP 403 for the aiacquisition scope, so the first failing build command line is not in hand. Sentry reads returned HTTP 403 for the same organization.

**Customer-facing blocker**: the build error text is the one thing the customer needs to repair his site, and no surface in the product exposes it.

**Unblock for a human**: someone with Vercel access reads the build events for the failed production deployment, identifies the first failing line, and either repairs the site so version 36 publishes or passes the error text to the customer.

relatedSnapshot.title: If node branch routing broken: edges missing branch data due to actionType mismatch
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Bug

When a user connects edges from an If (Condition) node, the edges are never tagged with `data.branch = 'true'/'false'`. This causes the executor to fall into the wrong code path, breaking conditional routing.

## Root Cause

`workflow-canvas.tsx` has three edge-creation handlers (`handleConnectionToExistingNode`, the drop-on-canvas handler, and `handleConnect`). All three check:

```ts
sourceNode?.data.config?.actionType === 'If'
```

But the If node is registered in `SYSTEM_ACTIONS` with `id: 'Condition'`, so the stored `actionType` is always `'Condition'`, never `'If'`. The `isIfNode` check therefore always evaluates to `false`, `branchData` is always `undefined`, and edges are created without `data.branch`.

## Impact

In `workflow-executor.ts`, the executor checks `edge.data?.branch === 'true'` / `'false'` to route execution:

* When condition is `true` and no branch data → **all** outgoing edges run (ignores false branch)
* When condition is `false` and no branch data → **nothing runs** — the false branch is silently skipped

Any workflow using an If node has broken conditional logic. The false branch never executes.

## Fix

Change the `isIfNode` check in all three edge-creation handlers in `workflow-canvas.tsx` from:

```ts
sourceNode?.data.config?.actionType === 'If'
```

to:

```ts
sourceNode?.data.config?.actionType === 'If' ||
sourceNode?.data.config?.actionType === 'Condition'
```

This matches the executor's own check at line \~1548–1550 which already handles both values.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI Name 7: preview/demo link is broken on every generation (new link per version, emitted before build finishes, never auto-updates)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The preview/demo link produced by the website creation step is unreliable on every generation, which blocks any automated "send the client their preview link" flow (e.g. the embedded form → AI → Name 7 → OAuth email notification pipeline).

Concretely:

1. **New link per version** — every version of the website creates a *new* demo link instead of a stable URL for the site. There is no single canonical preview URL we can hand to a client.
2. **Link emitted before the build finishes** — the website creator outputs the demo link *before* the site has finished building, so the link errors every time it is opened immediately after generation.
3. **No auto-update** — once emitted, the link does not automatically update to point at the finished/working build. It stays broken.

## Why it matters

We want automated sending of the preview link as part of the Name 7 workflow. Right now any automated notification would send a dead link. This is the blocker for closing that loop.

## Possible workaround

We *could* auto-publish the site on every generation as a workaround, so there is always a live published URL to share. Needs a decision on whether auto-publish-on-every-version is acceptable vs. fixing the preview-link lifecycle properly.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

* A stable preview/demo URL per website that survives across versions, OR a clearly-defined published URL we can rely on.
* The link is only surfaced once the build is actually viewable (or it resolves to a "building…" state instead of an error).
* The link auto-updates to the latest finished build.

## Related

* ENG-10093 (harden publish flow for failed Vercel deployments / misleading domain success states) — adjacent publish-reliability work.

relatedSnapshot.title: Replace the Fin ticket-association machinery with the minimal version
relatedSnapshot.description:
PR #138 delivered ENG-13769 but built far more machinery than the outcome needs. This ticket replaces it with the minimal version and records what was deliberately cut.

PR #138 is being closed unmerged. PR #139 builds forward from #137 on `afragahaha/fix-codex-over-engineer`.

## Why #138 is being replaced

#138 added roughly 900 lines, a `fin_cases` table, migrations `0008` and `0009` with a partial unique index, two-phase creation and document reservations, a reconciliation pass, and a third HTTP endpoint for status. Filing one ticket cost seven Name 1 calls and five database writes.

All of it exists to guarantee a Name 1 ticket is never filed twice. But the Intercom conversation ID is already written into the Name 1 issue description and link attachment, so it is already the idempotency key, and Name 1 is already the source of truth for whether a ticket exists. Searching before creating covers the same ground.

The second store also introduced a real defect that review caught: existing-ticket detection searched Name 1 full text and ignored the `fin_cases` rows, so the two could disagree. There was nothing to disagree with before the table existed.

## What ships instead

* One structured decision from the model: `not-needed` with a reason, or `file` with title, summary, customerSummary, project, assignee, classification and priority.
* `not-needed` returns with zero provider calls.
* `file` searches Name 1 by the Intercom conversation ID scoped to the Engineering Team. Zero matches creates once. One match returns `already-tracked`. More than one, or a paginated result, returns `failed` without guessing.
* The issue is read back once and verified before any success claim: description and link attachment each carry exactly one Intercom conversation ID and it is this conversation's, the issue URL matches its own identifier, and project, assignee, priority and labels match the decision. Any mismatch returns `failed`.
* Four outcomes preserved: `newly-created`, `already-tracked`, `not-needed`, `failed`.
* Filing costs at most three Name 1 calls. Exactly one `save_issue` call site, never retried.
* The report is written into the issue description atomically at creation. No separate Triage investigation document, no `save_document` or `get_document`.
* The outcome is saved inside the existing `outcome` jsonb on the existing `fin_investigation_runs` row. No new table, no new column, no new migration.
* The customer payload carries the outcome and message but never the ENG identifier. The internal Slack receipt keeps it.
* Status follow-up is a no-argument tool in the Fin lane, scoped to the session's own conversation, at most two Name 1 calls, returning a customer-safe sentence and never the identifier or a Name 1 URL.

## Deliberately not built

* `fin_cases` table and migrations `0008` / `0009`. Migrations stay at `0007`.
* Creation and document reservations, and the reconciliation pass. A lost race costs one duplicate ticket a human closes in seconds.
* `POST /internal/fin/case`. A status question in the chat is an ordinary turn.
* Cross-chat status lookup, `case_reference`, `previous_status`, the `unchanged` response, and the multi-case clarification flow.

ENG-13769's original acceptance asked for fresh-chat follow-ups and multi-case clarification. This slice ships same-conversation status only. Reopen that scope when a real customer asks from a fresh chat.

## Acceptance

`pnpm validate` clean, `pnpm build && pnpm verify:built-github` passing with the 31 GitHub definitions, and unit coverage for: not-needed short-circuit, create-once on zero matches, already-tracked on one match, failed on two matches, failed on routing mismatch, failed on source mismatch, and abort rethrow.

Fin stays Preview-only. Both scheduled support flags stay false. Live Preview acceptance against the exact deployed SHA is still required and is not claimed by local validation.

## Follow-up worth its own ticket

The bespoke Fin capability lane from #135 is the upstream cause of this pattern: it strips Foreman to almost nothing and re-grants capabilities one slice at a time, which is why every customer question becomes an engineering slice with its own store and doc. Collapsing it to normal Foreman minus model-authored SQL and raw Executor, with reads filtered by the verified organization ID, should be its own ticket before more is built on top.

relatedSnapshot.title: Impersonation Mode Showing Admin Data and Causing Navigation Errors
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Issue Identified

When an Admin uses Impersonation mode and moves between multiple user profiles, parts of the app continue showing **the Admin’s own data** instead of the impersonated user’s data:

* The **Offer Creator**
* **Growth Plan Creator**

These tools pre-populate with **admin data**, not the impersonated user’s data. In video, an Admin shows how they're impersonating a user but seeing their own Admin data in Growth Plan Creator:

Jam | Console logs, network requests, and more

Also, when admins are using Impersonation Mode, sometimes they see a 404 page. To get around this, they have to press the Back to Home button each time they see this page.

### Steps to reproduce: 

1. From the Admin page, impersonate as user
2. Stop impersonating that user
3. Impersonate another user
4. Observe the 404 error

**Workaround**: Admins can press the Back to Home button.

 <image> 

**Possible cause**: Browser caching keeping previous impersonation URLs in memory, and keeping the Admin's own data in memory.

## Expected Behavior:

Admins should be able to view user's accounts from Impersonation mode exactly how the user views their account: showing the user's data, not the Admin's data.

---
